sentences.en: As the discussion over how to address climate change heats up this Earth Day, we're taking a look at how people understand the risks of climate change and how they adapt.
sentences.zh: 随着地球日到来，关于如何应对气候变化的讨论愈发激烈，我们今天将探讨人们如何理解气候变化的风险以及如何进行适应。

sentences.en: In this episode, we talk with two psychologists who study everything from communication to behavior change
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们采访了两位心理学家，他们研究的领域涵盖了从沟通到行为改变的方方面面，

sentences.en: and discuss how psychological research can contribute to an understanding of global climate change.
sentences.zh: 并讨论了心理学研究如何有助于理解全球气候变化。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这里是《心理学谈话》节目。

sentences.en: Janet Swim is a professor of psychology at the Pennsylvania State University.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特·斯威姆是宾夕法尼亚州立大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: She chaired the American Psychological Association Task Force on Psychological Perspectives on Climate Change.
sentences.zh: 她曾担任美国心理学会气候变化心理学视角特别工作组的主席。

sentences.en: She's currently examining how people's beliefs about climate change are influenced by others, as well as how to encourage people to support pro-environmental behaviors.
sentences.zh: 她目前正在研究人们对气候变化的信念如何受到他人的影响，以及如何鼓励人们支持环保行为。

sentences.en: Also with us is John Fraser.
sentences.zh: 与我们一同出席的还有约翰·弗雷泽。

sentences.en: He is a conservation psychologist, architect, and educator, serving as president and CEO for the New York think tank, New Knowledge Organization.
sentences.zh: 他是一位保护心理学家、建筑师和教育家，现任纽约智库“新知识组织”的总裁兼首席执行官。

sentences.en: His current research focuses on how social relationships and media influence how people choose to engage
sentences.zh: 他目前的研究重点是社会关系和媒体如何影响人们的选择，

sentences.en: in solving big social problems like climate change mitigation, resolving health disparities, or creating positive opportunities for youth to become their best selves.
sentences.zh: 从而参与解决气候变化减缓、消除健康差异或为年轻人创造实现自我价值的积极机会等重大社会问题。

sentences.en: They are working together with the National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation,
sentences.zh: 他们正与“国家海洋与气候变化解释网络”合作，

sentences.en: which has the goal of training educators on how to effectively communicate climate change information.
sentences.zh: 该网络的目标是培训教育工作者如何有效地传播气候变化信息。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Swim and Dr. Fraser.
sentences.zh: 欢迎斯威姆博士和弗雷泽博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: First and foremost, this is the most basic question, but how is psychology contributing to the discussion about climate change?
sentences.zh: 首先，这是一个最基本的问题，心理学在气候变化的讨论中发挥了什么作用？

sentences.en: Well, I would say that there are probably two major ways that psychology is contributing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为心理学主要通过两个重要途径做出贡献。

sentences.en: One way is that a lot of psychologists look into behavioral change, and so there are issues about getting individuals to change everyday behaviors
sentences.zh: 一方面，许多心理学家研究行为改变，因此涉及到如何促使个人改变日常行为，

sentences.en: and individuals to engage in civic action, contacting their political officials and things like that.
sentences.zh: 以及促使个人参与公民行动，例如联系他们的政治官员等等。

sentences.en: The other is a broader perspective and bringing in issues of environmental justice and thinking about the ways that climate change affect people, minority groups,
sentences.zh: 另一方面是更广阔的视角，引入环境正义问题，思考气候变化如何影响人们、少数群体，

sentences.en: people in vulnerable parts of the world, both in the United States, actually, and across the planet.
sentences.zh: 以及世界各地（实际上包括美国境内和全球范围）弱势地区的人们。

sentences.en: I think there's been a lot of conversation about how people understand the facts of climate change, but very little about how we process it in our minds,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于人们如何理解气候变化的事实已经有很多讨论，但关于我们如何在心理上处理这些信息却知之甚少，

sentences.en: and that is really going to be key to any kind of future change, and that's where psychologists can be really useful.
sentences.zh: 而这对于未来的任何变革都至关重要，这正是心理学家可以发挥巨大作用的地方。

sentences.en: Are people's behaviors changing when it comes to taking steps to help prevent climate change, such as being more energy conscious, recycling?
sentences.zh: 在采取措施预防气候变化方面，比如更有节能意识、进行回收利用，人们的行为在改变吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think they have changed.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为他们已经改变了。

sentences.en: It's a slow movement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个缓慢的过程。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen all at once, but you can see things across the country.
sentences.zh: 它不会一蹴而就，但你可以在全国各地看到一些变化。

sentences.en: And even at our universities, there are lots more committees being formed and task force and trying to change institutions that way.
sentences.zh: 即使在我们的大学里，也成立了更多的委员会和工作组，试图以这种方式改变机构。

sentences.en: So I think we actually are seeing a lot of change in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们实际上在美国看到了很多变化。

sentences.en: I think it's such a big question about what you can do, that when people think at small levels like turning off lights or recycling,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于你能做什么的问题太大了，以至于当人们从关灯或回收利用这种小层面去思考时，

sentences.en: they're really not systemically organizing it in their minds about how can they deal with the biggest problem,
sentences.zh: 他们并没有在头脑中系统地组织起如何应对这一重大问题，

sentences.en: because it's pretty overwhelming when we start to think about the scale of climate change and what our little actions are going to be.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们开始思考气候变化的规模以及我们微小的行动将产生什么影响时，这确实令人感到不知所措。

sentences.en: But these collective actions are really starting to show.
sentences.zh: 但这些集体行动确实开始显现成效了。

sentences.en: Why do some people reject the notion of climate change occurring at all?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人完全拒绝气候变化正在发生这一概念？

sentences.en: Is there some sort of psychological reasoning behind this?
sentences.zh: 这背后有什么心理学原因吗？

sentences.en: Well, I definitely think there is some psychological reasoning behind it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我绝对认为这背后有心理学原因。

sentences.en: I think there's two conversations there in that question that I think it's important to unpack.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个问题中包含两个值得剖析的层面。

sentences.en: The first is that there aren't that many people who really deny climate change.
sentences.zh: 首先，真正否认气候变化的人其实并不多。

sentences.en: It's about 5% of our country doesn't think it's possible.
sentences.zh: 我们国家大约只有5%的人认为它是不可能的。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people who are questioning whether climate change or what the mechanisms are, but it's not denial.
sentences.zh: 有很多人在质疑气候变化本身或其机制，但这并不是否认。

sentences.en: That's a kind of propaganda story.
sentences.zh: 那是一种宣传手段。

sentences.en: I mean, 8% of America thinks Elvis is still alive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国有8%的人认为猫王还活着。

sentences.en: So it's not really a fact that people don't get it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们不理解它并不是事实。

sentences.en: It's understanding how it works.
sentences.zh: 关键在于理解它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So we're arguing over facts that everyone agrees on.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是在争论每个人都同意的事实。

sentences.en: What the real issue is, is that how do people understand climate change in their lives and practically how they can relate to the topic?
sentences.zh: 真正的问题在于，人们如何在生活中理解气候变化，以及他们如何实际地与这个话题建立联系？

sentences.en: I also say that part of the issue is that people are not talking about climate change either.
sentences.zh: 我还想说，部分问题在于人们也没有在谈论气候变化。

sentences.en: And so there's a part of the message when people think that other people are not believing in climate change, then they think that they don't want to be the ones to say something.
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们认为其他人不相信气候变化时，他们就不想成为那个开口说话的人，这传达了一种信息。

sentences.en: But actually a lot of people do.
sentences.zh: 但实际上很多人是相信的。

sentences.en: And so they need to just start talking about it with each other and start figuring out what it means for them
sentences.zh: 所以他们只需要开始互相谈论它，并开始弄清楚这对他们意味着什么，

sentences.en: and what they can do, what they can't do, what they're feeling like they're able to do.
sentences.zh: 以及他们能做什么、不能做什么，他们觉得能够做什么。

sentences.en: I mean, that's really the heart of our research, is how do we get people engaged in a conversation and something that is proactively imagining themselves in the solution
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是我们研究的核心，即如何让人们参与对话，并主动想象自己参与解决方案，

sentences.en: instead of pretending no one believes it, and there we just don't talk about it so we don't know where to go.
sentences.zh: 而不是假装没人相信它，从而导致我们不谈论它，以至于不知道该往哪里走。

sentences.en: And it has been politicized.
sentences.zh: 而且它已经被政治化了。

sentences.en: That's probably the biggest problem, is that facts have been politicized.
sentences.zh: 这可能是最大的问题，即事实已经被政治化了。

sentences.en: And one of the things that the National Network for Ocean Climate Change Interpretation is trying to do is take the politics away and get it back to practical action.
sentences.zh: “国家海洋与气候变化解释网络”试图做的一件事就是消除政治色彩，回归到实际行动中。

sentences.en: And how can psychologists inform policy discussions in this area?
sentences.zh: 心理学家如何为该领域的政策讨论提供信息？

sentences.en: One of the biggest roles for psychologists is really how do we talk about what is possible, what is our potential future.
sentences.zh: 心理学家最大的作用之一，确实是探讨什么是可能的，什么是我们潜在的未来。

sentences.en: When we think about policy, I mean, I'll tell you, our research is funded by the National Science Foundation.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论政策时，我得告诉你，我们的研究是由国家科学基金会资助的。

sentences.en: We are not involved in policy discussions in our research.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究并不涉及政策讨论。

sentences.en: But when I think as an individual about policy, one of the things psychologists can certainly do is help people understand what they can be as a political actor,
sentences.zh: 但当我以个人身份思考政策时，心理学家肯定能做的一件事是帮助人们理解他们可以成为什么样的政治参与者，

sentences.en: someone who is advocating for positive change that's going to make the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 成为一个倡导积极变革、让世界变得更美好的人。

sentences.en: That's my individual opinion, not the project, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这是我个人的观点，而不是项目的观点。

sentences.en: I would also say that there's a thing that psychologists can do is to help policymakers understand what people are thinking and feeling about climate change
sentences.zh: 我还想说，心理学家可以做的一件事是帮助政策制定者了解人们对气候变化的想法和感受，

sentences.en: and be part of the communication to tell policymakers that people are concerned about this and to be that voice and to make them realize that there's that concern.
sentences.zh: 并参与沟通，告诉政策制定者人们对此感到担忧，成为那种声音，让他们意识到这种担忧的存在。

sentences.en: A lot of policy focuses on things that are economic in structure, but we get concerned about issues of justice
sentences.zh: 很多政策关注的是经济结构方面的问题，但我们关心的是正义问题，

sentences.en: because there are people who are going to lose just because of where they live, how they live, or where they are in the economic spectrum.
sentences.zh: 因为有些人仅仅因为他们居住的地方、生活方式或在经济谱系中的位置而遭受损失。

sentences.en: And one of the things that we know from the general population is most people really care and want people to be protected.
sentences.zh: 我们从普通民众那里了解到，大多数人确实关心并希望人们得到保护。

sentences.en: They want to live in a peaceful society.
sentences.zh: 他们希望生活在一个和平的社会里。

sentences.en: They don't want conflict.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要冲突。

sentences.en: And so if we continue to talk about economics and not about the justice for people who are frontline living in places that are going to be threatened,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们继续谈论经济，而不谈论那些生活在受威胁地区的前线人民的正义问题，

sentences.en: like people who live in Micronesia, then we really aren't being good people.
sentences.zh: 比如生活在密克罗尼西亚的人们，那么我们真的不是好人。

sentences.en: So I think we can get engaged in those kind of policy decisions.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们可以参与到这些政策决策中。

sentences.en: How can psychologists improve communication about the very real impacts of climate change and what people can do to help address the threat?
sentences.zh: 心理学家如何改善关于气候变化现实影响的沟通，以及人们可以做些什么来帮助应对这一威胁？

sentences.en: You know, it's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Our research started long before Janet and I were collaborating.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究在珍妮特和我合作之前很久就开始了。

sentences.en: I was working for a conservation organization, the Wildlife Conservation Society in New York City, and we found that in our meetings there was a very elevated sense of concern,
sentences.zh: 我当时在纽约市的野生动物保护协会工作，我们发现会议中有一种非常强烈的担忧感，

sentences.en: almost what looked like panic in some conversations.
sentences.zh: 在某些对话中几乎看起来像是恐慌。

sentences.en: That started a project that eventually got sewed into the project we're working on today.
sentences.zh: 这开启了一个项目，最终融入了我们今天正在进行的项目中。

sentences.en: We were looking at the emotional experience of knowing the problem.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正在研究了解这一问题后的情感体验。

sentences.en: And climate change is really a threatening issue.
sentences.zh: 气候变化确实是一个威胁性的问题。

sentences.en: People see the world around them changing and leaving them, and that is emotionally distressing when you know the facts.
sentences.zh: 人们看到周围的世界在改变并离他们而去，当你了解事实时，这在情感上是令人痛苦的。

sentences.en: When you can see the evidence, it is distressing.
sentences.zh: 当你能看到证据时，这是令人痛苦的。

sentences.en: And when you think people around you don't believe you, you self-edit because the emotional labor that goes into doing that work is difficult.
sentences.zh: 当你认为周围的人不相信你时，你会进行自我审查，因为进行这种工作所付出的情感劳动是困难的。

sentences.en: So what we find is that people who know the facts, who understand what's necessary, who are working in frontline conservation jobs, who are working as educators,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，那些了解事实、明白必要性、在保护一线工作、担任教育工作者的人，

sentences.en: are emotionally distressed and avoiding the emotional labor of getting involved in the work.
sentences.zh: 在情感上感到痛苦，并试图避免参与这项工作所带来的情感劳动。

sentences.en: What we're trying to do is help these folks to see that there is a possible future,
sentences.zh: 我们试图做的是帮助这些人看到未来是有可能的，

sentences.en: there is a possible narrative, and I think this is a real job across the many different kinds of psychology, from positive psychology to consumer psychology to justice to peace.
sentences.zh: 叙事是有可能的，我认为这是跨越心理学许多不同分支的一项真正的工作，从积极心理学到消费心理学，再到正义与和平。

sentences.en: All of these topics deal with emotionally difficult work, and I think we need to focus on the worker's personal life and experience as part of that story,
sentences.zh: 所有这些主题都涉及情感上困难的工作，我认为我们需要关注工作者的个人生活和经历，将其作为故事的一部分，

sentences.en: not just about telling the story, but what does it mean to be a storyteller.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是关于讲述故事，还要关注作为讲述者意味着什么。

sentences.en: When I was doing that research, Janet Swim was working for the APA's task force on how does psychology address climate change,
sentences.zh: 当我进行那项研究时，珍妮特·斯威姆正在为美国心理学会关于心理学如何应对气候变化的工作组工作，

sentences.en: and I realized that she had some information that I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我意识到她掌握了一些我不知道的信息。

sentences.en: And so I called Janet and said, I would love to collaborate with you on this question because I don't know how to deal with this issue of emotional stress.
sentences.zh: 所以我打电话给珍妮特说，我很想在这个问题上与你合作，因为我不知道如何处理这种情感压力的问题。

sentences.en: That's an interesting perspective because I felt like I was there doing research on emotional issues about climate change, and I was looking for a place to do that research.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的视角，因为我觉得我当时正在研究关于气候变化的情感问题，并且我正在寻找一个地方来进行这项研究。

sentences.en: So I thought I had contact you and you to figure out if this would seem like a great place to do that research.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我应该联系你，看看这里是否是一个进行这项研究的好地方。

sentences.en: But the research that I was interested in, one of the emotions I was interested in is hope.
sentences.zh: 但我感兴趣的研究中，我感兴趣的情绪之一是希望。

sentences.en: And so hope is basically transforming fear into a positive experience in a sense that you have a sense that you know what you can do.
sentences.zh: 所以希望基本上是将恐惧转化为一种积极的体验，即你有一种知道自己能做什么的感觉。

sentences.en: You need basic fear to start with in a sense of why you want to be concerned about this and what you want to, you know, facing the future.
sentences.zh: 你需要基本的恐惧来开始，即你为什么想要关注这一点，以及你想要，你知道，面对未来。

sentences.en: But when you can start thinking about your ability to do something, having a plan of action, not necessarily a big plan of action, but have a plan for how you can talk to people,
sentences.zh: 但当你开始思考自己做某事的能力时，有一个行动计划，不一定是一个宏大的行动计划，但有一个关于如何与人交谈的计划，

sentences.en: then you can not feel so threatened.
sentences.zh: 那么你就不会感到那么受威胁了。

sentences.en: You can feel like you have some agency.
sentences.zh: 你可以感觉到自己有一些能动性。

sentences.en: And so working with these people in the zoos and aquariums seemed like an opportunity to take this feelings of threat
sentences.zh: 因此，与动物园和水族馆的这些人一起工作，似乎是一个机会，可以利用这种受威胁的感觉，

sentences.en: and help them see a plan of action and be able to then start having conversations with other people.
sentences.zh: 帮助他们看到一个行动计划，并能够开始与其他人进行对话。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about what that work is within the zoos and the aquariums?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈在动物园和水族馆里的这项工作是什么吗？

sentences.en: We're working with the National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation.
sentences.zh: 我们正在与“国家海洋与气候变化解释网络”合作。

sentences.en: That's a National Science Foundation-funded project organized by the New England Aquarium.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由新英格兰水族馆组织的、由国家科学基金会资助的项目。

sentences.en: But it's really a vision about creating a community of practice in the zoo and aquarium community.
sentences.zh: 但这实际上是一个关于在动物园和水族馆社区建立实践社区的愿景。

sentences.en: It's bringing in people who are doing this interpretation from around the country, working with an organization called Frameworks Institute,
sentences.zh: 它汇集了来自全国各地从事这种解释工作的人，与一个名为“框架研究所”的组织合作，

sentences.en: who are helping structure conversation that is depoliticized and about an interaction between two people on a topic they both are concerned about.
sentences.zh: 他们正在帮助构建一种去政治化的对话，关于两个人都关心的话题之间的互动。

sentences.en: And that project, what's exciting about it is it's an unusual training program.
sentences.zh: 而那个项目，令人兴奋的是它是一个不同寻常的培训项目。

sentences.en: We suggested when the project was first getting off the ground that instead of bringing one person to training, that we bring them with someone they work with every day,
sentences.zh: 我们在项目刚起步时建议，与其带一个人去培训，不如带上他们每天一起工作的人，

sentences.en: that they come in twos, that they work together on the problem-solving, and that they've got somebody who's got their back in their own office.
sentences.zh: 让他们成双成对地来，一起解决问题，并且在他们自己的办公室里有支持他们的人。

sentences.en: And those people work together in small groups of ten organizations.
sentences.zh: 这些人以十个组织为一组进行工作。

sentences.en: Those people work together in groups of twenty, two people from each organization on developing strategies that are unique to their local community.
sentences.zh: 这些人以二十人为一组，每个组织两人，共同制定针对他们当地社区的独特策略。

sentences.en: So this project that is zoos, aquariums, nature centers, people who are doing science interpretation around the country are starting to develop techniques and tools,
sentences.zh: 所以这个项目，包括动物园、水族馆、自然中心，全国各地从事科学解释的人们开始开发技术和工具，

sentences.en: but they're doing it with friends.
sentences.zh: 但他们是和朋友一起做的。

sentences.en: They're doing it with coworkers.
sentences.zh: 他们是和同事一起做的。

sentences.en: And that's part of why the psychological aspects of this are so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这方面的心理学方面如此有趣的部分原因。

sentences.en: Because what we're starting to see in some of the work that Janet's leading with looking at hope is that it is about those social interactions
sentences.zh: 因为我们在珍妮特领导的一些关于希望的研究中开始看到，这与那些社会互动有关，

sentences.en: and feeling that someone can experience what you're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 并且感觉到有人能体验到你正在经历的事情。

sentences.en: So part of this is bringing your friends along, but also what you start doing when you go back to your organization again.
sentences.zh: 所以这部分是带上你的朋友，但也包括当你回到你的组织时开始做的事情。

sentences.en: And so it's about the social networks that people have within the organizations, the social networks that they have with their friends and family outside of the organization.
sentences.zh: 所以这关乎人们在组织内部拥有的社交网络，以及他们在组织外与朋友和家人拥有的社交网络。

sentences.en: And then even when they go in and they give a program at a zoo and aquarium or in other informal science learning centers,
sentences.zh: 甚至当他们去动物园和水族馆或其他非正式科学学习中心进行项目时，

sentences.en: that the people they talk to hopefully will start talking to other people as well.
sentences.zh: 他们交谈的人希望也会开始与其他人交谈。

sentences.en: So it's large networks, but starting at a small scale with the people who actually are on the front line education.
sentences.zh: 所以这是大型网络，但从小规模开始，与那些真正处于一线教育的人一起。

sentences.en: When you think about ideas like a disease,
sentences.zh: 当你想到像疾病这样的想法时，

sentences.en: a good idea can migrate around, but it requires multiple contacts.
sentences.zh: 一个好的想法可以在周围迁移，但这需要多次接触。

sentences.en: People tend to be resistant to a single contact, but multiple exposure to an idea creates a greater opportunity for it to migrate, to move in society.
sentences.zh: 人们往往对单一接触有抵触情绪，但多次接触一个想法会创造更大的机会让它迁移，在社会中传播。

sentences.en: So when we think about people working in local zoos, aquariums, nature centers around the country, they talk to people every day.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们想到全国各地在当地动物园、水族馆、自然中心工作的人时，他们每天都在与人交谈。

sentences.en: Their best friends are their go-to folks for different topics.
sentences.zh: 他们最好的朋友是他们处理不同话题的首选对象。

sentences.en: So when you work in a zoo or aquarium, you're the go-to on nature questions.
sentences.zh: 所以当你在动物园或水族馆工作时，你是自然问题的首选专家。

sentences.en: So our stories about climate change are going to come through social networks, through people we truSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们关于气候变化的故事将通过社交网络，通过我们信任的人传播。

sentences.en: And those one-time visitors may take away a bit of an idea, but the people you talk to in your social life every day, every week, when you call mom and dad,
sentences.zh: 那些一次性的游客可能会带走一点想法，但你在日常生活中、每周、当你给父母打电话时交谈的人，

sentences.en: those are the conversations that really have a chance to pick up around the country and move at a bigger level.
sentences.zh: 那些才是真正有机会在全国范围内引起共鸣并在更大层面上推动的对话。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for joining us, Dr. Swim, Dr. Fraser.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常感谢你们加入我们，斯威姆博士，弗雷泽博士。

sentences.en: This has been very, very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常有意思。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: For more information on Dr. Swim's and Dr. Fraser's work, and to read the report of the American Psychological Association Task Force on Psychology and Global Climate Change,
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多关于斯威姆博士和弗雷泽博士工作的信息，并阅读美国心理学会心理学与全球气候变化特别工作组的报告，

sentences.en: visit our website at speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association, speaking of psychology,
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学会的《心理学谈话》节目，

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。
